bib.title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows", Ze Liu, Yutong Lin, Yue Cao, Han Hu, Yixuan Wei, Zheng Zhang, Stephen Lin, Baining Guo (Microsoft Research Asia). The PDF is arXiv:2103.14030v2, dated 17 Aug 2021. The PDF does not print a venue, so treat it as a preprint for citation unless the venue is checked somewhere else.

COVERAGE: 67,942 of 67,942 chars read. That covers the body, Tables 1-10, appendices A1-A3 (including the Table 7 architecture spec, the Table 8 input-size results and the Table 10 Swin-Mixer results), and references [1]-[85], which I skimmed. Nothing was skipped.

CLAIMS
- claim: Global attention cost grows with the square of the patch count, while window attention cost grows linearly once the window size M is fixed.
  number: Ω(MSA)=4hwC²+2(hw)²C; Ω(W-MSA)=4hwC²+2M²hwC; M=7
  setup: Image of h×w patches, channel dim C, M×M patches per window. Softmax is left out of the count.
  quote: "Ω(MSA) = 4hwC 2 + 2(hw)2C, (1) Ω(W-MSA) = 4hwC 2 + 2M 2hwC, (2) where the former is quadratic to patch number hw, and the latter is linear whenM is ﬁxed (set to 7 by default)." and "3We omit SoftMax computation in determining complexity."
  where: p4, Sec 3.2
- claim: Attention inside fixed windows has no links between windows. Swin alternates regular and shifted partitions in consecutive blocks, with the shift set to half a window, so information crosses window borders.
  number: shift of (⌊M/2⌋,⌊M/2⌋)
  setup: Example in Fig 2: an 8×8 map split into 2×2 windows of 4×4 (M=4).
  quote: "the next mod- ule adopts a windowing conﬁguration that is shifted from that of the preceding layer, by displacing the windows by (⌊ M2⌋,⌊ M2⌋) pixels from the regularly partitioned windows."
  where: p4
- claim: Hierarchy works like a CNN pyramid. A 4×4 patch embedding comes first, then each patch-merging layer concatenates 2×2 neighbours and applies a linear layer, which cuts the token count by 4 and doubles the channels. The four stages output at strides 4, 8, 16 and 32.
  number: 4×4×3=48 dims per patch; H/4 → H/8 → H/16 → H/32
  setup: All variants. Table 7 gives Swin-T at 224² input as 56×56 → 28×28 → 14×14 → 7×7.
  quote: "we use a patch size of 4× 4 and thus the feature dimension of each patch is 4× 4× 3 = 48" and "This reduces the number of tokens by a multiple of 2× 2 = 4 (2× downsampling of resolution), and the out- put dimension is set to 2C."
  where: p3, Sec 3.1; Table 7 p10
- claim: Shifted windows beat fixed windows on all three tasks.
  number: +1.1% top-1, +2.8 box AP / +2.2 mask AP, +2.8 mIoU
  setup: Swin-T. ImageNet-1K top-1; COCO with Cascade Mask R-CNN; ADE20K with UperNet. Table 4 numbers: 80.2→81.3, 47.7→50.5, 43.3→46.1.
  quote: "Swin-T with the shifted window partitioning outperforms the coun- terpart built on a single window partitioning at each stage by +1.1% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K, +2.8 box AP/+2.2 mask AP on COCO, and +2.8 mIoU on ADE20K."
  where: p8, Sec 4.4, Table 4
- claim: Relative position bias beats both no position encoding and absolute position embedding. Adding absolute embedding helps classification a little but hurts dense tasks.
  number: +1.2%/+0.8% top-1; +1.3/+1.5 box AP; +2.3/+2.9 mIoU; abs adds +0.4% cls, -0.2 AP, -0.6 mIoU
  setup: Swin-T, same three benchmarks as Table 4. The bias B∈R^{M²×M²} is taken from a learned table of size (2M−1)×(2M−1).
  quote: "Swin-T with rela- tive position bias yields +1.2%/+0.8% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K, +1.3/+1.5 box AP and +1.1/+1.3 mask AP on COCO, and +2.3/+2.9 mIoU on ADE20K in relation to those without position encoding and with absolute position embedding, respectively" and "while the inclusion of absolute position embedding improves image classiﬁcation accuracy (+0.4%), it harms object detection and semantic segmentation (-0.2 box/mask AP on COCO and -0.6 mIoU on ADE20K)."
  where: p8
- claim: ImageNet-1K top-1 with no extra pretraining data, compared with DeiT at similar compute.
  number: Swin-T 81.3 (29M, 4.5G, 755.2 img/s); Swin-S 83.0; Swin-B 83.5 at 224² and 84.5 at 384²
  setup: Trained on ImageNet-1K alone for 300 epochs with AdamW. Single-crop top-1. Throughput measured on a V100 with timm. Note that the prose says Swin-B is 83.3% at 224², but the Table 1 row reads 83.5. Table 8 also gives 83.3, so the paper is internally inconsistent here.
  quote: "+1.5% for Swin-T (81.3%) over DeiT-S (79.8%) using 224 2 input, and +1.5%/1.4% for Swin-B (83.3%/84.5%) over DeiT-B (81.8%/83.1%)" and "Swin-B 2242 88M 15.4G 278.1 83.5"
  where: p6, Table 1(a)
- claim: Pretraining on ImageNet-22K raises top-1, and Swin-L reaches 87.3%.
  number: Swin-B 86.4 (384², 47.0G, 84.7 img/s); Swin-L 87.3 (384², 197M, 103.9G, 42.1 img/s); ViT-B/16 84.0
  setup: Pretrained on ImageNet-22K (14.2M images, 22K classes, 90 epochs), then fine-tuned on ImageNet-1K for 30 epochs. V100 throughput.
  quote: "Swin-B obtains 86.4% top-1 accuracy, which is 2.4% higher than that of ViT with similar inference throughput (84.7 vs. 85.9 images/sec) and slightly lower FLOPs (47.0G vs. 55.4G). The larger Swin-L model achieves 87.3% top-1 ac- curacy"
  where: p6, Table 1(b)
- claim: Best COCO result is 58.7 box AP and 51.1 mask AP on test-dev.
  number: 58.7 / 51.1; +2.7 box AP, +2.6 mask AP over the prior best
  setup: Swin-L (284M) with HTC++ (instaboost, 6x schedule, soft-NMS, an extra global self-attention layer, ImageNet-22K init) and multi-scale testing. Without multi-scale testing it scores 57.7/50.2.
  quote: "Our best model achieves 58.7 box AP and 51.1 mask AP on COCO test-dev, surpassing the previous best results by +2.7 box AP (Copy-paste [26] without exter- nal data) and +2.6 mask AP (DetectoRS [46])."
  where: p7, Table 2(c)
- claim: With the detection framework held fixed, Swin-T beats ResNet-50 and DeiT-S as a backbone. DeiT is slower because its attention is quadratic.
  number: +3.4∼4.2 box AP over R-50; Swin-T 50.5 AP at 15.3 FPS vs DeiT-S 48.0 at 10.4 FPS
  setup: COCO val; Cascade Mask R-CNN, ATSS, RepPointsV2 and Sparse R-CNN; 3x schedule. DeiT-S gets deconvolution layers added to make it hierarchical.
  quote: "Our Swin-T architecture brings consistent +3.4∼4.2 box AP gains over ResNet-50" and "signiﬁcantly higher inference speed (15.3 FPS vs. 10.4 FPS). The lower inference speed of DeiT is mainly due to its quadratic complexity to input image size."
  where: p7
- claim: ADE20K segmentation reaches 53.5 mIoU on val.
  number: 53.5 mIoU (+3.2 over SETR's 50.3); Swin-S 49.3 vs DeiT-S 44.0
  setup: UperNet. Swin-L is pretrained on ImageNet-22K, trained at 640×640 input and tested multi-scale. It has 234M params, 3230G FLOPs and runs at 6.2 FPS.
  quote: "Our Swin-L model with ImageNet-22K pre-training achieves 53.5 mIoU on the val set, surpassing the previous best model by +3.2 mIoU (50.3 mIoU by SETR [81] which has a larger model size)."
  where: p8, Table 3
- claim: Shifted windows run much faster than sliding-window attention for about the same accuracy. The cyclic-shift batching beats padding.
  number: 40.8×/2.5× down to 7.6×/1.8× per stage; whole model 4.1/1.5× faster; cyclic gives a 13%/18%/18% speed-up over padding
  setup: V100 GPU, Table 5. Sliding-window Swin-T scores 81.4 vs 81.3 for shifted (Table 6).
  quote: "The self-attention modules built on the proposed shifted window approach are 40.8 ×/2.5×, 20.2×/2.5×, 9.3×/2.1×, and 7.6×/1.8× more efﬁcient than those ofslid- ing windows in naive/kernel implementations on four net- work stages" and "Overall, it brings a 13%, 18% and 18% speed-up on Swin-T, Swin-S and Swin-B"
  where: p8
- claim: Swin is slightly faster than Performer and more accurate.
  number: +2.3% top-1 (81.3 vs 79.0)
  setup: Swin-T on ImageNet-1K, Tables 5-6.
  quote: "achieving +2.3% top-1 accuracy compared to Performer on ImageNet-1K using Swin-T"
  where: p8
- claim: Higher input resolution gives higher accuracy at lower throughput. This is the resolution-cost tradeoff relevant to the token-count section of the note.
  number: Swin-T 81.3 at 755.2 img/s (224²) → 82.2 at 219.5 img/s (384²)
  setup: ImageNet-1K, Table 8. Models at higher resolutions are fine-tuned from the 224² model.
  quote: "2242 81.3 755.2 83.0 436.9 83.3 278.1" and "3842 82.2 219.5 83.9 127.6 84.5 84.7"
  where: Appendix A3.1, p10
- claim: Shifted windows naive padding would grow the window count from 2×2 to 3×3. Cyclic shift with masking keeps the window count unchanged.
  number: 2.25×
  setup: Shifted configuration when the regular partition has few windows.
  quote: "the increased computation with this naive solution is considerable (2× 2→ 3× 3, which is 2.25 times greater)."
  where: p5
- claim: Applying the hierarchy and shifted windows to MLP-Mixer also helps.
  number: 81.3% vs 76.4%; no-shift Swin-Mixer-B gets 80.3
  setup: ImageNet-1K at 224². Swin-Mixer-B/D24 uses 10.4G FLOPs vs 12.7G.
  quote: "Swin-Mixer performs signiﬁcantly better than MLP-Mixer (81.3% vs. 76.4%) using slightly smaller computation budget (10.4G vs. 12.7G)."
  where: Appendix A3.3, p11

LIMITS:
- The authors concede the speed comparison is unfair to Swin: "ResNe(X)t is built by highly optimized Cudnn functions, our architecture is implemented with built-in PyTorch functions that are not all well-optimized. A thorough kernel optimization is beyond the scope of this paper."
- The linear-complexity claim is analytical. It leaves out softmax, and it assumes M is fixed. Throughput is measured only on one V100. There is no latency or memory sweep across image sizes that would show the linear scaling empirically. Table 8 only goes from 224² to 384².
- The headline SOTA numbers come from heavy recipes: ImageNet-22K pretraining, HTC++ with an extra global self-attention layer, and multi-scale testing. The gaps are smaller under like-for-like setups.
- Baselines: ResNe(X)t was retrained with AdamW instead of its default SGD (Table 9). DeiT had deconvolution layers added so it could be used for detection.
- The paper shows no use in vision-language or LLM pipelines, despite its "unified modeling" motivation. NLP use is listed as future work. It also does not test whether the patch tokens are suitable for feeding a language model.
- Dated: this is 2021 work. Its ImageNet, COCO and ADE20K SOTA claims have since been passed, and the throughput numbers are V100-era.

BUILDS ON: Transformer (Vaswani et al. 2017 [64]); ViT (Dosovitskiy et al. 2021 [20]); DeiT training recipe (Touvron et al. 2020 [63]); relative position bias following [49, 1, 32, 33] (Raffel et al. 2020; Bao et al. 2020; Hu et al. 2018; Hu et al. 2019); local or sliding-window self-attention (Hu et al. 2019 [33]; Ramachandran et al. 2019 [50]); hierarchical CNN feature maps (VGG [52] 2015, ResNet [30] 2016, FPN [42] 2017, U-Net [51] 2015); concurrent PVT (Wang et al. 2021 [66]), noted as still quadratic; MLP-Mixer (Tolstikhin et al. 2021 [61]); Performer (Choromanski et al. 2021 [14]).

CODE: The PDF has no code listings. These are the load-bearing equations, verbatim.
- Eq. 3, p4: "ˆzl = W-MSA (LN (zl−1)) + zl−1, zl = MLP (LN (ˆzl)) + ˆzl, ˆzl+1 = SW-MSA (LN (zl)) + zl, zl+1 = MLP (LN (ˆzl+1)) + ˆzl+1"
- Eq. 4, p5: "Attention(Q,K,V ) = SoftMax(QK T/√d +B)V"
- Variants, p5: "Swin-T: C = 96, layer numbers ={2, 2, 6, 2} • Swin-S: C = 96, layer numbers ={2, 2, 18, 2} • Swin-B: C = 128, layer numbers ={2, 2, 18, 2} • Swin-L: C = 192, layer numbers ={2, 2, 18, 2}". Head dim d=32, MLP ratio 4, window M=7.
- Code is at github.com/microsoft/Swin-Transformer.

FIGURES:
- Fig 1, p1: "(a) The proposed Swin Transformer builds hierarchical feature maps by merging image patches... linear computation complexity... (b) In contrast, previous vision Transformers [20] produce feature maps of a single low resolution and have quadratic computation complexity". This side-by-side of the Swin pyramid and ViT's flat token grid explains the token-count difference faster than prose, so it is the best fit for "What the model actually sees".
- Fig 2, p2: shifted window illustration, layer l regular and layer l+1 shifted. It shows at a glance how information crosses window boundaries.
- Fig 3, p4: Swin-T architecture with patch partition, linear embedding, 4 stages of 2/2/6/2 blocks and patch merging, plus the paired W-MSA/SW-MSA blocks. Useful for the hierarchy.
- Fig 4, p5: cyclic shift plus masked MSA batching. Only worth showing if implementation detail matters.

PROBLEMS:
- In the extraction, subscripts and superscripts are flattened. "H4× W4" means H/4×W/4, "2242" means 224², and "C 2" means C². I copied the quotes as extracted.
- Table 7 and the figure diagrams came out as interleaved text, but they could be read.
- The paper contradicts itself on Swin-B at 224² from ImageNet-1K training: the prose and Table 8 say 83.3, Table 1(a) says 83.5.
- The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
- The venue is not printed in the PDF.
